The Economy That Never Moved Online
For thirty years, we watched commerce move online. Except it didn't. What moved online was the easy stuff: books, clothes, electronics. Things you buy without asking a single question.
Everything else stayed where it was.
A hydraulic crane. An industrial roofing contract. A plasma cutting machine. Anything worth $5,000 to $1 million is still sold the way it was sold in 1990: through conversations between people. A buyer calls. They ask whether the machine holds torque at 8,000 RPM, whether it clears a load spec, whether a custom alloy can ship in three weeks. Someone who knows the answer talks them through it. Then a deal happens.
The internet never captured this economy because the knowledge needed to close these sales was never on the internet. It lives in spec sheets, PDF catalogs, a rep's inbox, and an engineer's head. Software could build catalogs, carts, and checkouts. It could not hold a conversation. So the largest, highest-value category of commerce simply skipped the internet era.
That just changed, for two reasons.
First, buyers moved. They now ask ChatGPT and Claude the questions they used to ask Google, and increasingly, the questions they used to ask a sales rep. Soon their AI agents will do the research, shortlisting, and negotiating for them. The buying side of this economy is going agentic fast.
Second, AI can finally do the one thing software never could: conversation. It can absorb everything a business knows, the catalogs, the calls, the tribal knowledge, and answer a nuanced technical question the way a good rep would.
When both of those are true, an entire economy comes online at once.
That's what we're building at Gushwork. We take everything a seller knows and make it legible to AI: readable by agents, citable by assistants, answerable in the moment a buyer asks. We are building the storefront for the agentic web.
There are more than 35 million of these businesses across our focus markets and more than 100 million worldwide. They make and move the physical things everything else depends on. They didn't miss the internet because they were behind. They missed it because the internet wasn't ready for them.
Now it is.
